title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 245
paragraphs: Sailing from this city, you will come to the “Deserters” in another period of time equal to that in which you came from Elephantine to the mother-city of the Ethiopians. The name of these “Deserters” is Asmach, and this word, when translated into the tongue of the Hellenes, means “those who stand on the left hand of the king.” These were two hundred and forty thousand Egyptians of the warrior class, who revolted and went over to the Ethiopians for the following cause. In the reign of Psammetichus garrisons were stationed — one towards the Ethiopians at the city of Elephantine, another towards the Arabians and Assyrians at Daphnae of Pelusium, and another towards Libya at Marea. Even in my own day the garrisons of the Persians are ordered in the same way as these were under Psammetichus, for both at Elephantine and at Daphnae the Persians have outposts. The Egyptians of whom I speak had served as outposts for three years and no one relieved them from their guard; accordingly they took counsel together, and adopting a common plan they all in a body revolted from Psammetichus and set out for Ethiopia. Hearing this, Psammetichus set out in pursuit, and when he overtook them he entreated them much and tried to persuade them not to desert the gods of their country, their children, and their wives. At this, it is said, one of them pointed to his genitals and said that wherever this was, there they would have both children and wives. When they came to Ethiopia they gave themselves over to the king of the Ethiopians; and he rewarded them thus: there were certain of the Ethiopians who had come to be at odds with him, and he bade these men drive them out and dwell in their land. So when these men settled in the land of the Ethiopians, the Ethiopians have come to be of milder manners, having learnt the customs of the Egyptians.
